shared_elements: large upright stone slab/monolith displayed in a museum setting
carved/incised decoration on a single broad face
prominent circular disc motif centred on the surface
horizontal band dividing the upper part of the surface
roughly bilateral symmetry about a vertical axis
flanking vertical elements framing the central field
justification: The most specific correspondence is that both are tall upright stone slabs whose broad face is organised symmetrically around a single prominent disc set below a horizontal banded zone, with curling/scrolled forms at the sides. The biggest difference is the manner of carving and subject: A is a deeply modelled, weathered, quasi-anthropomorphic mass with a headdress-like top and blurred forms, whereas B is a flat panel covered in crisp, thin, evenly incised linear spirals and interlace with no bodily reference.
